title: Automated eval rollback service for variant rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a low-latency, automated safety net for rolling model/config changes that can detect functional regressions in near real-time and trigger safe rollbacks. Current rollouts rely on manual review of eval dashboards and ad-hoc alerts; this causes delayed rollbacks and customer exposure to regressions.

Goal:
Build an automated service that evaluates canary and A/B variants against production baselines using curated prompt sets and user-seeded telemetry, applies configurable statistical checks (effect-size + distribution tests), and performs an automated rollback when preset thresholds are breached. The system must be auditable, reversible, and provide clear signal to SRE/PM/SEs.

Requirements and constraints:
- Must operate for both config-only changes (e.g., sampling/temperature/batching) and model variant swaps.
- Work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with pluggable telemetry sinks.
- Default rollout policy: 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> 50% -> 100% with pause windows; automated evaluation windows apply at each step.
- Evaluation window: min 1,000 scored requests OR 30 minutes, whichever is earlier for initial canary; longer windows for higher traffic customers.
- Primary checks: quality delta on baseline eval score (absolute and relative thresholds), regression of hammer prompts, increase in hallucination rate, broken structured-output regressions, p95 latency regressions > 30% vs baseline.
- Action on breach: immediate traffic cutover to last known-good variant, create incident ticket, capture eval artifacts, and notify owners via PagerDuty/Slack.
- Support per-customer thresholds and opt-outs for sensitive customers.

Non-goals:
- End-to-end model training or automatic model selection.
- Replacing manual deep-dive QA for ambiguous alerts.

Observability and audit trail:
- Every automated decision must store: evaluation snapshot, metric deltas, trigger rule used, and the last 5 checkpoints.
- Provide UI in Console to inspect rollback reasons, view diff-sets for prompts that failed, and re-run evals on-demand.

Security & compliance:
- Telemetry snapshots must be scrubbed for PII before storing; for Private deployments allow customers to configure retention and encryption settings.

Deliverables:
- Eval-rollback microservice with gRPC/HTTP API for registering rollouts and querying status.
- Comparator library used by runtime to stream sample requests and score them against eval harness.
- Console dashboard + audit log entries.
- Integration test suite and a dry-run mode that performs detection without acting.
acceptance_criteria: Service can register and monitor a 1% canary and produce evaluation results within 30 minutes for medium-traffic services.
Automatic rollback triggers when quality delta & latency thresholds are exceeded using default thresholds (configurable per project).
Console shows an auditable rollback event with snapshot links and links to the PR/deploy that triggered the rollout.
Dry-run mode correctly flags regressions without changing routing; results validated by PM QA team on two example models.
End-to-end integration tests covering Hosted and Dedicated flows are green in CI with PR coverage >= 80% for core comparator logic.
Security review completed and telemetry scrubber enabled by default; Private deployments respect customer retention settings.
implementation_steps: Spike: implement lightweight comparator that scores 500 sample prompts against baseline and variant (complete - 2026-02-20).
Design: finalize trigger rule DSL (stat tests, effect-size, hysteresis) and per-customer override model — design doc approved 2026-02-26.
Build: eval-rollback microservice + persistent audit store (Postgres + S3 for artifacts).
Integrate: runtime hook to stream first-N requests to comparator with sampling policy and KV cache warmup handling.
Console: add rollback events panel and per-rollout timeline with links to failing prompts and diff view.
QA: create synthetic regression scenarios and run against staging; enable dry-run for 48h on low-traffic production customers.
Rollout: enable default for internal teams, then opt-in for customers; collect feedback and iterate thresholds.
risks: False positives from small sample sizes causing unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated via hysteresis and minimum sample thresholds.
KV cache warmup differences between variants producing apparent regressions — require warmup-aware sampling and per-variant warmup windows.
Performance overhead on runtime if sampling policy not tuned — we'll use lightweight scoring and offload heavy analysis to the microservice.
Storage/perf cost of storing eval artifacts long-term — retention policy and configurable S3 lifecycle rules planned.

2026-03-09 — QA: dry-run started against canary of internal search feature; initial alerts flagged harmless formatting changes — adjusted tokenizer-aware checks.
